root_cause_summary: ANSWERABILITY_CONSTRAINT_GUARD_V1 modeled GE(25) entailment using numeric monotonicity: it treated evidence_op=ABOVE (i.e., GT) as satisfying required_op=AT_LEAST (GE). This assumes the policy fact is monotone over a single numeric value, ignoring the boundary inclusion difference where evidence GT(25) excludes exactly 25 from the policy scope.

code_level_cause.logic_snippet: if kind == "AT_LEAST": return evidence_at_least or evidence_above or evidence_exact
why_it_breaks: The guard interprets evidence operator ABOVE as satisfying AT_LEAST.
But under the required boundary-semantics model, GT(25) is an open lower bound (values > 25), while GE(25) is a closed lower bound (values >= 25).
Therefore GT(25) does NOT entail GE(25) for policy scope questions that depend on whether the boundary value 25 is included.

implications: The fix must replace V1's monotone entailment shortcut with an explicit relational boundary semantics model (EQ/GT/GE/LT/LE and BEFORE/AFTER/ON) that respects open vs closed boundaries.
